interfaces.name: Model for the data
interfaces.type_shape: Original deterministic signal plus stationary centered noise model, with positive finite long-run variance. Signals need not be piecewise constant after the change.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original deterministic signal plus stationary centered noise model, with positive finite long-run variance. Signals need not be piecewise constant after the change.

members.statement_original:
Suppose we are given noisy data of the form
\[
X_t=\mu_t+Z_t,\qquad t=1,\ldots,n,\tag{1}
\]
where $\mu_t$ are means or signals and $(Z_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ is a stationary process with mean $0$, auto-covariance function $\gamma(k)=\operatorname{Cov}(Z_{t+k},Z_t)$, and finite long-run variance
\[
0<\sigma_\infty^2:=\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty}\gamma(k)<\infty.\tag{2}
\]

naming_context.text: Model for the data and the problems considered.

interfaces.name: Long-run variance
interfaces.type_shape: Original two-sided covariance-sum variance of the stationary centered noise. It is explicitly positive; do not replace it by marginal variance or assume independent observations.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original two-sided covariance-sum variance of the stationary centered noise. It is explicitly positive; do not replace it by marginal variance or assume independent observations.

members.statement_original:
auto-covariance function $\gamma(k)=\operatorname{Cov}(Z_{t+k},Z_t)$, and finite long-run variance
\[
0<\sigma_\infty^2:=\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty}\gamma(k)<\infty.\tag{2}
\]

interfaces.name: Null hypothesis
interfaces.type_shape: Original constant-mean null with unrestricted common level.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original constant-mean null with unrestricted common level.

members.statement_original:
Consider the following null hypothesis
\[
H_0:\mu_1=\cdots=\mu_n,\tag{3}
\]
where the signal is constant (i. e., all means $\mu_j$ are equal, but not necessarily zero)

interfaces.name: Alternative hypothesis
interfaces.type_shape: Original one-sided irregular-signal alternative. Tau indexes the first changed observation; d is a lower gap bound, not necessarily an attained minimum.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original one-sided irregular-signal alternative. Tau indexes the first changed observation; d is a lower gap bound, not necessarily an attained minimum.

members.statement_original:
the alternative hypothesis
\[
H_1:\exists\tau\in\{2,\ldots,n\},d>0:\mu_1=\cdots=\mu_{\tau-1},\quad\mu_\tau,\ldots,\mu_n\ge\mu_1+d,\tag{4}
\]
where the signal is constant for the first $\tau-1$ observations and the means from the $\tau$th observation onward may then vary arbitrarily as long as they are larger by at least $d$.

interfaces.name: Consistent estimator
interfaces.type_shape: Original generic variance-estimator requirement for the test, also explicitly required by Theorem 3.3. It does not force the optional canonical estimator (8).
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original generic variance-estimator requirement for the test, also explicitly required by Theorem 3.3. It does not force the optional canonical estimator (8).

members.statement_original: and $\hat\sigma_\infty^2$ is a consistent estimator for the long-run variance $\sigma_\infty^2$, defined in (2).

interfaces.name: Testing procedure
interfaces.type_shape: Original lower-tail minimum CUSUM statistic, using the full-sample mean and a consistent long-run standard deviation estimate. It is not the maximum absolute CUSUM.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original lower-tail minimum CUSUM statistic, using the full-sample mean and a consistent long-run standard deviation estimate. It is not the maximum absolute CUSUM.

members.statement_original:
We use the following quantity:
\[
\hat T:=\min_{j=1,2,\ldots,n}\sum_{i=1}^j(X_i-\bar X_n)/(\sqrt n\hat\sigma_\infty),\qquad\text{where }\bar X_n:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nX_i,\tag{5}
\]

interfaces.name: Sample means
interfaces.type_shape: Original nonoverlapping block means and block-size regime. A final incomplete block is not included in R_1 through R_m.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original nonoverlapping block means and block-size regime. A final incomplete block is not included in R_1 through R_m.

members.statement_original:
To reduce the noise from the data and to focus our attention on the signal, we will, here and in the following sections, split the data set into $m:=\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ blocks of size $k$ where $k\to\infty$ and $k/n\to0$. Then we calculate the blocks’ sample means as follows:
\[
R_j:=\frac1k\sum_{i=(j-1)k+1}^{jk}X_i,\qquad j=1,2,\ldots,m.\tag{6}
\]

interfaces.name: Index
interfaces.type_shape: Original minimum-block index and selected prefix endpoint. Tie-breaking is not specified; the later fixed-J alternative is kept separate.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original minimum-block index and selected prefix endpoint. Tie-breaking is not specified; the later fixed-J alternative is kept separate.

members.statement_original:
From the $R_j$ we then obtain
\[
\hat L:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{i=1,\ldots,m}R_i,\qquad\hat\ell:=k\hat L,\tag{7}
\]
where $\hat L$ indicates an index of a block likely to have all observations in it prior to the change point and $\hat\ell$ points to the last observation in the $\hat L$th block.

interfaces.name: Preliminary estimate
interfaces.type_shape: Original selected-prefix sample mean, using ell_hat from (7). The initial centering mean is distinct from the later improved muhat_1.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original selected-prefix sample mean, using ell_hat from (7). The initial centering mean is distinct from the later improved muhat_1.

members.statement_original:
\[
\hat\mu_0:=\frac1{\hat\ell}\sum_{i=1}^{\hat\ell}X_i,
\]

interfaces.name: Overlapping block averages
interfaces.type_shape: Original sliding average indexed by s/k, which need not be an integer; its window ends at s.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original sliding average indexed by s/k, which need not be an integer; its window ends at s.

members.statement_original:
\[
R_{s/k}:=\frac1k\sum_{i=s-k+1}^sX_i,
\]
where the definition of the overlapping block averages $R_{s/k}$ extends the one for the non-overlapping blocks in (6)

interfaces.name: Estimate for long-run variance
interfaces.type_shape: Original data-selected overlapping-block variance estimator, the specific estimator studied by Theorem 3.2. It is an optional choice in (5) and (9), not automatically required there.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original data-selected overlapping-block variance estimator, the specific estimator studied by Theorem 3.2. It is an optional choice in (5) and (9), not automatically required there.

members.statement_original:
To estimate the long-run variance, we suggest
\[
\hat\sigma^2:=\frac k{\hat\ell-k+1}\sum_{s=k}^{\hat\ell}(R_{s/k}-\hat\mu_0)^2,\tag{8}
\]

interfaces.name: Standard normal distribution
interfaces.type_shape: Original normal-quantile convention for blockwise decisions. The choice 1-1/m tends to one; it is not the Brownian-bridge cutoff for the global test.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original normal-quantile convention for blockwise decisions. The choice 1-1/m tends to one; it is not the Brownian-bridge cutoff for the global test.

members.statement_original: The quantity $z_\alpha$, $\alpha\in(0,1)$, denotes the $\alpha$th-quantile of the standard normal distribution, and $m:=\lfloor n/k\rfloor$, as before.

interfaces.name: Test statistics
interfaces.type_shape: Original standardized blockwise statistic using the preliminary mean and any consistent variance estimator.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original standardized blockwise statistic using the preliminary mean and any consistent variance estimator.

members.statement_original:
\[
\hat D_j:=\sqrt k(R_j-\hat\mu_0)/\hat\sigma_\infty
\]

interfaces.name: Test decisions
interfaces.type_shape: Original binary decision with an inclusive >= threshold. Requires m>=2 for a finite interior normal quantile.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original binary decision with an inclusive >= threshold. Requires m>=2 for a finite interior normal quantile.

interfaces.name: Fitting a step function
interfaces.type_shape: Original binary step-fit estimate of the coarse change block. Its argmin tie convention is unspecified.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original binary step-fit estimate of the coarse change block. Its argmin tie convention is unspecified.

naming_context.text: obtained by fitting a step function

interfaces.name: Preliminary estimates
interfaces.type_shape: Original improved prefix mean using eta_hat, not the initial minimum-block L_hat.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original improved prefix mean using eta_hat, not the initial minimum-block L_hat.

\hat\mu_1:=\frac1{k\hat\eta}\sum_{i=1}^{k\hat\eta}X_i,
\]

naming_context.text: Finally, we obtain the preliminary estimates

interfaces.name: Preliminary estimates
interfaces.type_shape: Original sliding-block gap estimate. The source later says it estimates d_star, not necessarily the pointwise lower bound d. No empty-minimum fallback is stated.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original sliding-block gap estimate. The source later says it estimates d_star, not necessarily the pointwise lower bound d. No empty-minimum fallback is stated.

interfaces.name: Locating Algorithm
interfaces.type_shape: Original refined location estimator. The criterion stops at j-1 while j denotes the first changed observation. Rho=1/2 is an optional rule of thumb, not the full theorem domain.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original refined location estimator. The criterion stops at j-1 while j denotes the first changed observation. Rho=1/2 is an optional rule of thumb, not the full theorem domain.

members.statement_original:
In this section we define the novel estimate for the time $\tau$ where the change occurs; cf. (4). Consider
\[
\hat\tau:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{j=2,\ldots,n}\sum_{t=1}^{j-1}(X_t-\hat\mu_1-\rho\hat d),\tag{12}
\]
where $\rho\in(0,1)$ is a tuning parameter.

interfaces.name: Causal stationary process
interfaces.type_shape: Original causal measurable-function representation driven by IID innovations; the observed noise process itself need not be independent.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original causal measurable-function representation driven by IID innovations; the observed noise process itself need not be independent.

members.statement_original:
In this framework, we view the causal stationary process $(Z_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ as outputs from a physical system as follows
\[
Z_t=G(\ldots,\varepsilon_{t-1},\varepsilon_t),\tag{13}
\]
where $(\varepsilon_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$, i. i. d., is the input information of this system and $G$ is an $\mathbb R$-valued measurable function that can be thought of as a filter or, intuitively, “mechanism” of this system.

interfaces.name: Functional dependence measure
interfaces.type_shape: Original single-innovation coupling at time zero with its Ltheta norm. This is not pairwise covariance or a replacement of the entire past.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original single-innovation coupling at time zero with its Ltheta norm. This is not pairwise covariance or a replacement of the entire past.

members.statement_original:
Then with this system, we measure the dependence from how much the outputs of this system will change if we replace the input information at time $t=0$ with an i. i. d. copy $\varepsilon'_0$. Assume $\mathbb E|Z_i|^\theta<\infty$, $\theta\ge1$. For a single observation at time $i$, we define the functional dependence measure as follows:
\[
\delta_{i,\theta}=(\mathbb E|Z_i-Z_{i,\{0\}}|^\theta)^{1/\theta},\qquad\text{where }Z_{i,\{0\}}=G(\ldots,\varepsilon_{-1},\varepsilon'_0,\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_i).\tag{14}
\]

interfaces.name: Cumulative dependence measure
interfaces.type_shape: Original future-tail sum of functional dependence measures, with n=0 permitted.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original future-tail sum of functional dependence measures, with n=0 permitted.

members.statement_original:
To measure the temporal dependence for the whole time series, we define the cumulative dependence measure of $(Z_i)_{i\ge n}$ on $\varepsilon_0$:
\[
\Theta_{n,\theta}=\sum_{i\ge n}\delta_{i,\theta},\qquad n\ge0.\tag{15}
\]

interfaces.name: Condition 3.1
interfaces.type_shape: Complete original moment/dependence condition, including both theta regimes and exact logarithmic thresholds. Gamma_theta is an exponent, not the autocovariance gamma(k).
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Complete original moment/dependence condition, including both theta regimes and exact logarithmic thresholds. Gamma_theta is an exponent, not the autocovariance gamma(k).

members.statement_original:
$(Z_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$ satisfies that the $\theta$-th moment $H_\theta:=(\mathbb E|Z_i|^\theta)^{1/\theta}<\infty$, where $\theta>2$. Assume that any one of the following holds
• $\theta>4$ and $\Theta_{n,\theta}=O(n^{-\gamma_\theta}(\log n)^{-A})$, as $n\to\infty$, for $A>2(1/\theta+1+\gamma_\theta)/3$, where
\[
\gamma_\theta=(\theta^2-4+(\theta-2)\sqrt{\theta^2+20\theta+4})/(8\theta);
\]
• $2<\theta\le4$ and $\Theta_{n,\theta}=O(n^{-1}(\log n)^{-A})$, as $n\to\infty$, with $A>3/2$.

interfaces.name: Short-range dependence
interfaces.type_shape: Original summability condition in Theorem 3.1, weaker than the separate higher-moment Condition 3.1 used for the locating theory.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original summability condition in Theorem 3.1, weaker than the separate higher-moment Condition 3.1 used for the locating theory.

members.statement_original:
Assume that the short-range dependence condition holds:
\[
\Theta_{0,2}=\sum_{i\ge0}\delta_{i,2}<\infty.\tag{16}
\]

interfaces.name: Index of the last block
interfaces.type_shape: Original floor definition and its printed accompanying interval. The two conflict when tau is an exact multiple of k; retain the source wording and record that boundary issue.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original floor definition and its printed accompanying interval. The two conflict when tau is an exact multiple of k; retain the source wording and record that boundary issue.

members.statement_original: Denote by $\eta:=\lfloor\tau/k\rfloor$ the index of the last block for which the signal is still constant; i. e., $\eta k+1\le\tau\le(\eta+1)k$, where $\tau$ is the index of the change; cf. the alternative hypothesis (4) considered.

interfaces.name: Quantities
interfaces.type_shape: Original sequence-order and n-dependence convention. These are contextual bindings, not new model hypotheses; meanings of d,tau,k,m,eta are resolved separately.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original sequence-order and n-dependence convention. These are contextual bindings, not new model hypotheses; meanings of d,tau,k,m,eta are resolved separately.

members.statement_original: In the statement of the proof we write $a_n\ll b_n$ or $b_n\gg a_n$ to mean that $a_n=o(b_n)$, as $n\to\infty$. The quantities $d=d_n$ and $\tau=\tau_n$ are the ones from (4), which we allow to depend on $n$ without making this explicit in the notation, and $k$ is the user-chosen block size; cf. Section 2.3.1. Further, $m:=\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ and $\eta:=\lfloor\tau/k\rfloor$, as before.

interfaces.name: Minimum gap
interfaces.type_shape: Original minimum sliding-block signal gap after the true block index. It is not the same object as the pointwise lower bound d or its noisy estimate d_hat.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original minimum sliding-block signal gap after the true block index. It is not the same object as the pointwise lower bound d or its noisy estimate d_hat.

members.statement_original:
We provide this bound in terms of the minimum gap to the signal averaged over sliding blocks. More precisely, defining
\[
d_*:=\min_{i=k(\eta+1)+1,\ldots,n-k+1}\frac1k\sum_{j=i}^{i+k-1}(\mu_j-\mu_1),\tag{20}
\]
